title: Residents in Alberta community disturbed after fatal police-related shooting
article: The family of a man fatally shot by a Mountie near Ma-Me-O Beach on Saturday is now calling for justice.
But members of the small community have mixed emotions about what happened that fateful night, although details about the shooting have yet to be released.

"It's mixed emotions. They are a close group in the community, everybody knows each other. But I don't think the community is really going to get involved with this," said a man, who did not want to named for fear of retaliation.
"A lot of people in the community are scared of that family."
It was around 9:30 p.m. on Saturday when Wetaskiwin RCMP pulled over a vehicle on Highway 13A for an impaired driving investigation.

According to police, an altercation ensured and the lone officer shot two people - 32-year-old Lance Cutarm and his 41-year-old brother Laron Cutarm. Lance died at the scene and Laron was taken to hospital in stable condition.
The shooting is now being investigated by the Alberta Serious Response Team (ASIRT), but a spokesperson could not say if either of the men who were pulled over had weapons.
Heartbroken family members at the scene on Saturday called for justice.
"What they did was wrong. They didn't need to shoot him like that," said Lance's sister Lori Cutarm.
"My brother was very gentle. He may have all the tattoos to make him look bad, but he wasn't. He was a good guy."
In 2001, Lance was sentenced to three years behind bars for fatally stabbing Michael (Mikey) John Couterielle following a gang-related home invasion in Edmonton.
Couterielle was fatally stabbed in the chest when he went to a four-plex to investigate the commotion.
Lance was charged with second-degree murder, but pleaded guilty to manslaughter during his trial in May 2001.
Three years later, cops were on the hunt for Lance after he broke conditions of his release. Police called Cutarm an "active native gang member" at the time.
Ma-Me-O Beach is located approximately 100 km southwest of Edmonton.
The shooting marks the third incident within three days that ASIRT is now investigating.
